McCoy, G.A. and Douglass, J.G. (2014). Premium Efficiency Motor Selection and Application Guide: A Handbook for Industry. U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy, Advanced Manufacturing Office; prepared by Washington State University Energy Program with support from the Copper Development Association; published by NREL. DOE/GO-102014-4107, February 2014.

Locators are printed chapter-page numbers (e.g. p.4-12 = chapter 4 page 12, PDF page 62). Main file: full-load efficiency by class (old standard / NEMA Premium) for 5-200 hp from Table 4-6 (MotorMaster+ defaults); 75%-load efficiency of NEMA Energy Efficient vs NEMA Premium motors 10-500 hp (Table 4-1); purchase-price examples converted to USD/kW (250-hp energy efficient motor $13,500; 75-hp premium motor $4,640 + $330 installation); 25-year typical motor life; cast copper rotor motor efficiencies (Table 7-1). Part-load efficiencies, EISA minimums, efficiency history, motor population/hours, price premiums (15-30%), rewind losses in _other-values; per-motor annual savings (Tables 4-1, 4-2) in _measures. Not extracted: Appendix A (old standard efficiencies at 4 loads x 4 speeds x 2 enclosures) and Appendix B (complete NEMA EE/Premium minimum tables); Figure 4-1 repair vs new cost (chart, 2011 prices, no printed values); voltage and power-quality tables. TRAP, efficiency classes: the source's 'standard efficiency' = pre-EPAct = IEC IE1; 'energy efficient' = EPAct/NEMA EE = IE2; 'premium' = NEMA Premium = IE3 (p.2-7). The archetype motor_induction-standard is described as IE2-IE3 and motor_premium-efficiency as IE4-IE5, so NEMA Premium is mapped to motor_induction-standard, not motor_premium-efficiency. Efficiencies are motor-only (shaft out / electricity in), not system. Table 4-1 values are at 75% load, Table 4-6 main-file values at full load. Prices: no price year printed; publication year 2014 used.
